name: Rain of Fire
description: There are $$$n$$$ detachments on the surface, numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, the $$$i$$$-th detachment is placed in a point with coordinates $$$(x_i, y_i)$$$. All detachments are placed in different points. Brimstone should visit each detachment at least once. You can choose the detachment where Brimstone starts. To move from one detachment to another he should first choose one of four directions of movement (up, right, left or down) and then start moving with the constant speed of one unit interval in a second until he comes to a detachment. After he reaches an arbitrary detachment, he can repeat the same process. Each $$$t$$$ seconds an orbital strike covers the whole surface, so at that moment Brimstone should be in a point where some detachment is located. He can stay with any detachment as long as needed. Brimstone is a good commander, that's why he can create at most one detachment and place it in any empty point with integer coordinates he wants before his trip. Keep in mind that Brimstone will need to visit this detachment, too. Help Brimstone and find such minimal $$$t$$$ that it is possible to check each detachment. If there is no such $$$t$$$ report about it.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ $$$(2 \le n \le 1000)$$$ — the number of detachments. In each of the next $$$n$$$ lines there is a pair of integers $$$x_i$$$, $$$y_i$$$ $$$(|x_i|, |y_i| \le 10^9)$$$ — the coordinates of $$$i$$$-th detachment. It is guaranteed that all points are different.
output_specification: Output such minimal integer $$$t$$$ that it is possible to check all the detachments adding at most one new detachment. If there is no such $$$t$$$, print $$$-1$$$.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1419F — Rain of Fire [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
